title: Welcome to PlanetMusic: The Client-Side Vault
summary: An introduction to your new personal music library and how the client-side architecture keeps your data safe.
content:
Everyone have their own way of enjoying music. That is why PlanetMusic was built from the ground up to be a deeply personal, fully customizable client-side music player and lyrics engine.

Unlike traditional cloud services, the entire catalog of your saved songs and settings are kept securely right in your own browser.

---

## 1. The Cosmos vs The Vault

When you use the search bar, the system automatically fetches data from the **Cosmos** (our integration with public iTunes and Deezer databases). When you find a track you like, just click the **Add to Vault** button in the player modal.

Once a song is in your Vault, it is saved directly to your device's LocalStorage. You can then edit its metadata, assign high-resolution artist images, upload local MP3s, or completely rewrite the lyrics!

> **PRO TIP:** Because the app stores everything locally, you should regularly export your entire Vault as a JSON backup file using the download icon in the top right corner. Make sure to back up often!

## 2. No Accounts Required

Since the system runs entirely on your local machine, there are no usernames, passwords, or cloud accounts. Dive in, start searching the Cosmos, and build the ultimate personalized library!

title: How Player Audio Streams & Custom Links Work
summary: Learn how the player streams audio, matches reference track durations, formats custom links, and resolves Deezer URL redirects.
content:
The built-in player streams audio directly alongside your synced lyrics map. A combination of YouTube links, Deezer streams, and local files provide a seamless listening experience.

Here is how the player works and how to set up your audio sources.

---

## 1. Playing Music & Playback Controls

Controlling your track playback is fast and flexible:

* **Playback Buttons:** Click the **Play / Pause** button on the bottom player bar or control panel to start or stop the audio.
* **Keyboard Shortcut:** Press the **Spacebar** on your keyboard at any time to toggle playback instantly while working.
* **Scrubbing Timeline:** Click along the audio progress bar to jump directly to any part of the song.

---

## 2. Adding Local Audio Files

You do not need an online streaming link to play your music. You can load audio files directly from your device:

* **Selecting Local Audio:** Click the **Play Music From** field and choose the **Local File / File Upload** option.
* **Supported Local Formats:** Load standard files like `.mp3`, `.wav`, or `.m4a`.
* **Instant Speed:** Local files play immediately with zero network buffering.

---

## 3. Matching Song Duration

Before choosing or pasting an audio source, look at the track details on the dashboard:

> **CHECK THE DURATION:** Locate the track length listed **right beside the release date of the song**.

Songs often have multiple versions. Always pick an audio file or link that matches the **exact duration beside the release date**. If your audio stream is shorter or longer, your line timestamps will drift out of sync with the music.

---

## 4. Supported Platforms & Spotify Notice

You can paste external track links into your song settings:

* **Supported Sources:** YouTube Music URLs, full Deezer web addresses, and direct Local MP3 files.
* **Spotify Unsupported:** **Spotify links do NOT work.** Spotify enforces strict security and copyright protections that block external web players from playing their audio streams.

---

## 5. How to Format Deezer Links

Standard Deezer mobile or desktop share links **will not work** in the player because they are shortened share buttons rather than complete web addresses.

> **CRITICAL DEEZER WORKFLOW:** You must open shortened share links in a browser tab to get the full web address before pasting.

### Step-by-Step Deezer Guide:

1. In Deezer, click **Share** on the song and select **Copy Link**.
2. Open a new tab in your web browser, paste the share link into the address bar, and press **Enter**.
3. Wait a second for the page to finish loading so the full web address appears.
4. Copy that complete URL from your browser address bar and paste it into the player field.

---

## 6. Switching Audio Sources

Once you add your link or upload a file, click the **Play Music From** field to select or switch between your available audio sources anytime.

title: Formatting Lyrics & Singer Tags
summary: Learn how to format section headers with artist colons, duet lines, and ad-lib parentheses for automatic colors and splits.
content:
Formatting song lyrics lets the engine recognize which artist is singing each phrase and render unique singer colors in the preview window.

Here is how to map section headers, text styles, and pasted online lyrics to your vocalists.

---

## 1. Multi-Artist Section Headers

List up to **four artists** inside square brackets after a colon, assigning each vocalist a unique text style:

`[Verse: Artist 1, _Artist 2_, **Artist 3**, **_Artist 4_**]`

> **COLON RULE:** Only text **after the colon** is parsed for artist names. Header labels before the colon are ignored. If no colon exists `[Verse 1]`, the section **defaults to the primary track artist**.

---

## 2. The 4 Vocalist Text Styles

The mapping of these text weights to specific artists happen in real time:

1. **Plain Text** = Artist 1
2. **_Italics_** = Artist 2
3. **Bold** = Artist 3
4. **_Bold-Italics_** = Artist 4

### Example Setup

```text
[Verse: Artist 1, _Artist 2_, **Artist 3**, **_Artist 4_**]
Artist 1 sings this plain line, _(Artist 2 sings this italic adlib)_
**Artist 3 sings this bold line**, **_Artist 4 sings this bold-italic line_**
```

---

## 3. Multiline & Online Copy-Pasting

You do not always have to format text manually from scratch:

* **Understanding Online Lyrics:** Lyrics copied from sites like Genius or AZLyrics often come pre-formatted with italics for background vocals or bold text for featured artists. Pasting them into the editor automatically maps those styles to Artist 2, 3, or 4 based on your header!
* **Multiline Styling:** Text formatting works across multiple lines simultaneously. Wrapping five consecutive lines in `_italics_` or `**bold**` assigns that entire verse block to the corresponding artist at once.

---

## 4. Live Preview Window Verification

Check the **Live Preview Window** as you type or paste lyrics:

* **Dynamic Palette:** Each of the four text styles triggers a distinct artist theme color instantly.
* **Layout Shifts:** Lines render with their assigned weights, colors, and split layouts in real time so you can verify artist assignment before saving.

title: How to Search and Save Songs to Your Vault
summary: A simple guide to searching online databases, discovering music across the Cosmos, and saving tracks directly to your personal Vault.
content:
Searching for music and expanding your collection takes just a few clicks. You can filter through your saved songs or scan online databases across the entire music universe.

---

## 1. Searching Your Local Vault

The main search bar at the top of your dashboard filters your saved collection in real time.

* **Instant Filtering:** Start typing an artist name, song title, or keyword to filter your local cards immediately.
* **Resetting Your View:** Click the **Home** button in the top navigation bar to clear your active search query and return to your full collection view.

---

## 2. Searching the Cosmos

If a track is not in your saved collection, search online music databases using **Cosmos Search**.

1. Type the song title or artist name into the main search box.
2. Press **Enter** on your keyboard or click the **Search Icon** button.
3. The dashboard splits your view into **Vault** results and **Cosmos** results.
4. Online matches from public databases appear in the Cosmos column.

The fusion of duplicate tracks from different databases keep the interface incredibly clean and easy to navigate.

---

## 3. Adding Songs to Your Vault

Once you find the song you want in the search results, saving it takes one simple step:

* Open the track by clicking on its song card, then click **Add to Vault** at the bottom of the left control panel.

> **QUICK TIP:** Adding a track to your Vault automatically fetches available online lyrics and timing files so your song is ready to play immediately.

---

## 4. Where Saved Songs Go

Every saved track stays stored directly inside your **browser storage**.

* **Home Dashboard:** Saved songs appear permanently on your **main home dashboard**.
* **Instant Loading:** Tracks in your **Vault** load instantly without requiring a new search.

title: How to Sync Songs with Music
summary: Learn how to map line timestamps, use keyboard shortcuts, split and loop ad-libs, and switch audio sources.
content:
Syncing lyrics to music brings your songs to life with live scrolling and dynamic highlighting. The sequence of pressing the start and end markers dictate how smooth it looks in playback.

Here is your complete guide to using the sync workspace.

---

## 1. Essential Keyboard Shortcuts

Control your timing map using simple keyboard commands while the song plays:

* **`Spacebar`** : Plays or pauses audio playback.
* **`Down Arrow`** : Tap once to set the **Start** marker. Tap again to seal the **End** marker and jump to the next line.
* **`Up Arrow`** : Clears the current line timing and steps back to the previous line.
* **`Left` / `Right` Arrows** : Nudges audio position backward or forward by **1 second**.

---

## 2. Splitting & Syncing Ad-Libs

Background vocals, echoes, and chants wrapped in parentheses `(like this)` can be isolated by clicking **Split Adlibs**.

> **CRITICAL RULE:** Ad-lib timestamps live inside their parent line. An ad-lib **cannot extend past the end timestamp** of its main line.

Follow these four key rules when syncing ad-libs:

1. **Sync the Main Line First:** Map the main sentence before touching the ad-lib.
2. **Manual Click Required:** Standard line-by-line syncing with the `Down Arrow` **skips ad-lib lines entirely**. You must manually click an ad-lib line to select and sync it.
3. **Automatic Parent Looping:** Clicking an un-synced ad-lib line automatically **loops audio** between the start and end markers of its main line.
4. **Auto-Ending Shortcut:** Click the ad-lib line and tap `Down Arrow` **once** when the echo starts. Let the song play. The engine automatically assigns the main line's end marker to the ad-lib when playback reaches it.

---

## 3. Auto-Sync & Database Mapping

Save time by pulling pre-timed files from open databases:

* **Auto-Sync Lyrics:** Searches online libraries to fetch fully timed lyrics automatically.
* **Map Timings from Auto:** Transfers time markers from public databases directly onto your custom typed text.

---

## 4. Switching Audio Sources

Different audio files play at slightly different speeds or start points.

> **QUICK TIP:** Click directly on the **Source Badge Name** (YouTube, Deezer, or Local MP3) in the top bar to cycle through available audio feeds instantly.

title: Advanced Ad-lib Syncing & Orbital Layouts
summary: Explore how the Focused View dynamically calculates safe zones to orbit background vocals around the main lyric line.
content:
One of the crowning achievements of the PlanetMusic UI is the **Focused View**.

While Live View scrolls vertically like traditional karaoke, Focused View places the main lyric directly in the center of the screen. A series of background vocals and echoes require their own dedicated timeline and physical space to prevent overlapping.

---

## 1. The Collision Math

When a secondary artist sings an ad-lib, the engine dynamically spawns their text somewhere else on the screen. 

The orbital math calculates bounding boxes around the main text, the artist name watermark, and the edge of the screen. It then finds the largest "safe zone" where the ad-lib can fit without crashing into anything.

## 2. The Debug Overlay

If you want to see the math in action, open the Workspace Controls and click **Show Adlib Debug**.

This will overlay technical HUD metrics on the screen:
* **Green Boxes:** Represent the safe zones where text is allowed to spawn.
* **Dashed Lines:** Show the collision bounding boxes of the text elements.
* **Radial Lines:** Draw the distance and angle calculation from the center of the screen to the chosen spawn point.

## 3. Matrix Multi-Singer Mode

If a song has a massive ensemble cast (like a 5-person group singing at once), the engine divides the screen into a Matrix Grid (e.g. a 5x2 grid). 

The assignment of the artists to these quadrants follow a staggered mathematical pattern to prevent visual overlap. For five singers, the top row is physically arranged as `1 2 3 4 5`, while the bottom row shifts slightly to `2 3 4 5 1`. Each singer gets their own strict physical quadrant to ensure chaos doesn't ensue.

Check the Debug Overlay during a complex ensemble track to watch the quadrant assignment happen live!

title: How to Use the Translation Workspace
summary: Translate lyrics, refine pronunciation and CJK spacing, then save or export your draft.
content:
Translate lyrics, refine pronunciation, and prepare Japanese or Chinese spacing in one workspace. Review everything before saving it to your song.

---

## 1. Open and read the workspace

Open a song with lyrics and choose **Edit Translation**. Each row shows the original, a language tag, pronunciation when available, and an English translation field. Japanese (`ja`) and Chinese (`zh...`) rows also have a spacing field. Split ad-libs appear as indented rows.

The language tag starts as `auto`. Set a code such as `ko`, `ja`, `zh-CN`, `es`, or `en` if detection is wrong. `en` means the source is already English, so translation and pronunciation are cleared for that row.

---

## 2. Translate lines

Choose the method that fits the lyric:

* **Translate All** requests each row using its language tag, then fills translation and pronunciation where available. While it runs, this button becomes **Stop Translation**.
* **Translate with Context** groups rows by language and sends each group together to help preserve surrounding meaning. The context of the surrounding lines, particularly when translating poetry, determine the accuracy of the result.
* **Refresh a line** with its circular-arrow button to fetch a new result for only that row.

Translation targets English. Review names, slang, wordplay, and line breaks before saving.

---

## 3. Space Japanese and Chinese

For rows tagged `ja` or `zh...`, edit the **Spacing Field** or choose **Auto Spacing**. Auto Spacing estimates word breaks, preserves punctuation, and updates pronunciation for matching rows only. It can take longer than translation because it makes extra lookups.

Treat the result as a draft. Check names, particles, mixed Latin text, and punctuation. A non-empty spacing value becomes the input for later translation requests.

---

## 4. Edit, import, and export

Edit translation and pronunciation directly. **Export Text** downloads one blank-line-separated block per row.

**Import Text** matches blocks to rows by original lyric, ignoring case. If a lyric does not match, it falls back to that block's position, so keep blocks in order.

---

## 5. Save or reset

* **Save Changes** applies the draft to the song in your Vault and closes the workspace.
* **Cancel** asks before discarding unsaved edits.
* **Refresh Lyrics** clears translations, pronunciation, and spacing and resets language tags to `auto`; original lyrics stay intact.

title: Understanding the Auto-Spacing Engine for CJK
summary: Deep dive into how PlanetMusic uses reverse-alignment algorithms to inject spaces into continuous Chinese and Japanese scripts.
content:
Japanese and Chinese lack spaces between their words natively. While this is fine for reading, a karaoke-style music player needs to know exactly where words begin and end so it can highlight them in sync with the audio.

To solve this, we built the **Brute Force Engine** for Auto-Spacing.

---

## 1. Why is Spacing Hard?

When we send a Japanese line like `君の声が聞こえる` to a translation API, it returns a romanized payload like `Kimi no koe ga kikoeru`. The API gives us spaces in the English letters, but it does *not* tell us which Japanese character corresponds to which English word.

## 2. The Context Symbol Trick

To figure out the boundaries, the engine iterates over the line character by character from the end to the beginning. It asks the API to translate fragments of the sentence. 

However, translating a single isolated character often gives a totally different pronunciation than when it is inside a sentence! To force the API to read the character in context, the engine uses a musical note symbol `♫` as a delimiter.

It queries: `(君の声が聞こえる) ♫ る`
The API translates the full sentence, hits the musical note, and then gives us the contextual pronunciation for just `る`.

## 3. The Reverse Alignment

Once the engine figures out the pronunciation of every single character in context, it matches those fragments against the full romanized sentence. 

The alignment of the translated romanized words against the original characters take a few seconds to run, but when the fragments line up perfectly with a space in the romanized version, the engine knows to insert a space into the original text! 

The result is beautifully spaced characters: `君の 声が 聞こえる`.

title: The Image Manager: Customizing Artist Profiles
summary: How to set persistent high-resolution images and distinct colors for every artist in your Vault.
content:
In the Live and Focused lyrics view, the background smoothly crossfades between different artist photos depending on who is currently singing. 

By default, the system fetches artist images from Wikipedia. However, sometimes Wikipedia doesn't have a great photo, or you want to use a specific era's aesthetic. That is where the **Image Manager** comes in.

---

## 1. Accessing the Image Manager

Open any saved song in your Vault that has lyrics, and click **Manage Artists** on the left panel. 

This opens a list of every singer detected in your lyrics (based on your section headers and ad-lib tags).

## 2. Setting Global Assets

* **Image URLs:** Paste any direct image link (ending in .jpg, .png, etc.) into the text box. High-definition square images work best.
* **Artist Colors:** Click the color swatch next to the artist's name to assign a unique text color. 

The assignment of distinct colors and high-resolution images apply globally. If you set an image for an artist in one song, that exact image and color will automatically be used in *every* song in your Vault that features them. You only have to do it once!

## 3. Finding Good Images

Clicking on the artist's name in the manager will automatically open a DuckDuckGo image search for high-resolution square images. Just right-click an image you like, select "Copy Image Address", and paste it into the app.

title: Personalizing the Viewing Experience & Layout
summary: Tweak the typography, background opacities, and canvas proportions in the Settings tab.
content:
PlanetMusic is designed to look good on massive desktop monitors and tiny mobile screens alike. We exposed almost all of the CSS variables in the **Settings Tab** so you can tune it exactly how you want it.

---

## 1. Typography Controls

The typography settings adjust everything from the primary lyrics down to the phonetic transliterations. The selection of typography sizes and background opacities give you full control over legibility.

* **Live Font Size:** Scales the main text in the scrolling view.
* **Floating Adlib Size:** Controls how large the background vocals appear when they orbit the main text in Focused view.
* **Translation Spacing:** The sliders let you push the English translation higher above the text, and the Romaji pronunciation lower below the text, giving you perfect breathing room.

## 2. Layout Proportions

You can tweak the exact width of the song cards on the home screen, the padding inside them, and whether they have sharp or rounded corners.

If you prefer the lyrics to take up more space on the screen than the album art, adjust the **Modal Split Ratio** slider.

## 3. Ambient View

If you just want to leave music playing on a secondary monitor, go to Settings and click **Enter Ambient View**. This hides the entire track grid and search bar, leaving you with just the floating chat-bubble lyrics rising gracefully from the bottom of the screen while the music plays.

title: Data Storage, Backups & The Purge Button
summary: Understand where your data lives, how IndexedDB handles your MP3s, and why backing up is critical.
content:
Because PlanetMusic does not use centralized cloud servers, understanding how your browser stores your data is crucial to not losing your library.

---

## 1. LocalStorage vs IndexedDB

The app uses two different storage mechanisms in your browser:

* **LocalStorage:** This holds all your text data. Your song metadata, lyrics, timestamps, and app settings live here. It is lightning fast but has a size limit.
* **IndexedDB (`PlanetMusicDB`):** This is a heavy-duty binary database. Whenever you upload a Local MP3 file to play a song, it is stored in IndexedDB. The storage of binary audio blobs inside IndexedDB prevent the browser from crashing when you load massive libraries.

## 2. Exporting JSON Backups

Creating backups is important. In the top right corner of the navigation bar, there is a Download icon. 

Clicking this generates a `PlanetMusic_Backup.json` file containing your entire Vault's text data (lyrics, timings, settings). 

> **WARNING:** The JSON backup does *not* include your Local MP3 files or your Deezer ARL token. If you move to a new computer, you will need to re-upload your MP3s and re-enter your ARL.

## 3. The Purge Button

If you ever want to completely wipe the application from your device, go to **Settings** and click the big red **Purge All Local Data** button. 

This will permanently delete your LocalStorage, destroy the IndexedDB database containing your audio files, and reset the app. (It automatically downloads a JSON backup right before deleting, just in case you change your mind!).

title: Decoding the Live Equalizer & Web Audio
summary: How the Web Audio API tracks frequencies and powers the dynamic visualizer at the bottom of the screen.
content:
If you play a Local MP3 or a Deezer stream, you might notice the pulsing white bars at the bottom of the lyrics screen. That is the Live Equalizer.

---

## 1. How the Web Audio API Works

Unlike fake CSS animations, the equalizer is driven by real math. The engine intercepts the audio stream and passes it through the browser's `AudioContext`.

The Web Audio API monitors the signal using an `AnalyserNode`. The analysis of the audio frequencies, broken down into 64 distinct bins, create the visualizer you see on the screen.

## 2. The Visual Math

Each bar represents a specific frequency. The script applies an exponential curve to the data to make the bass spikes look more aggressive and dynamic.

> **NOTE ON YOUTUBE:** You will notice the equalizer does not appear when playing YouTube sources. This is because YouTube serves their audio in a locked cross-origin iframe. The browser's security policies strictly forbid the Web Audio API from analyzing cross-origin audio to prevent unauthorized data scraping.

If you find the equalizer distracting or it is draining your laptop battery, you can disable it entirely by checking **Disable Animations** in the Settings tab.

title: Troubleshooting Playback & Missing Artworks
summary: How to fix CORS errors, buffering loops, and missing album covers.
content:
Because PlanetMusic runs entirely in your browser without a central backend, it is at the mercy of your browser's security policies. 

Here are some common issues and how to fix them.

---

## 1. Missing Album Art (CORS Errors)

Sometimes an album cover will load as a broken image or a gray placeholder. This is usually due to CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing). 

If the server hosting the image refuses to let a third-party website (like PlanetMusic) read the image data, the enforcement of cross-origin resource sharing policies block the image from loading.

* **The Fix:** Open the Image Manager and paste a different image URL from a host that allows cross-origin requests (like Wikipedia or Imgur).

## 2. Deezer Buffering Loops

If you have a Deezer ARL entered but the audio just spins and says "Buffering stream" forever:

* Your ARL token may have expired. They usually last a few months.
* You might have copied the wrong cookie. Make sure you copied the cookie named exactly `arl`.
* Go to Settings, paste a fresh ARL, and click **Verify Token Status**.

## 3. Empty iTunes Search Results

If the Cosmos search returns zero results for a very famous song, Apple's search algorithm might just be confused by the formatting.

* **The Fix:** Try searching just the artist name, or removing terms like "(Remastered)" or "(feat. XYZ)" from your query.

title: Creating Custom Blogs & Workspaces
summary: A guide to creating your own markdown blogs and navigating the various workspaces.
content:
PlanetMusic is not just for music; it also includes a full Markdown blogging engine so you can document your translation notes, syncing strategies, or just personal thoughts.

---

## 1. The Creator Studio Workspace

When you navigate to the **Blog** tab and click the `+` button, you enter the Creator Studio. This workspace lets you draft articles using standard Markdown formatting. The rendering of headers, lists, and bold text happen as you type.

* **Title & Category:** Give your post a catchy title. The system fetches your tags to categorize it.
* **Markdown Magic:** You can use standard formatting like `**bold**`, `_italics_`, or blockquotes using `> `.
* **Live Preview:** As you type, the right side of the screen updates in real-time. 

> **PRO TIP:** You can paste images directly from your clipboard as URLs if you host them online, or use the toolbar buttons to inject syntax instantly.

## 2. Managing Your Workspaces

PlanetMusic runs on a modular workspace system:

* **Lyrics Editor:** For raw text manipulation and metadata entry.
* **Translation Workspace:** For phonetic transliterations and localized translations.
* **Sync Workspace:** For mapping timestamps to audio.
* **Image Manager:** To globally map HD images to specific artists.

Because everything runs client-side, make sure to save your work before closing a modal. The app usually warns you if you have unsaved changes, but it's always good practice to hit that save button!

title: Importing & Exporting Translations (.TXT)
summary: How to bypass the API entirely by importing your own custom translation files into the workspace.
content:
Sometimes you don't want to use Google Translate at all. If you found a great translation online, or you are fluent and wrote one yourself in a text editor, you can inject it directly into the app.

---

## 1. Exporting the Template

Inside the Translation Workspace, click **Export Text**. This will download a `.txt` file containing your original lyrics, broken down block by block.

Each block is separated by a blank line.

## 2. Formatting the Text File

Open the `.txt` file in any text editor. The parsing of these text blocks, including the language tags and transliterations, rely on strict blank lines.

A perfectly formatted block looks like this:

```text
[lang: ja]
君の声が聞こえる
Kimi no koe ga kikoeru
I can hear your voice
```

1. **Line 1 (Optional):** The language tag wrapped in brackets.
2. **Line 2:** The original lyric.
3. **Line 3 (Optional):** The phonetic transliteration.
4. **Line 4:** The English translation.

If you don't need a pronunciation line, just put the translation directly under the original lyric. 

## 3. Importing Back to the App

Once you are done editing your `.txt` file, click **Import Text** in the Translation Workspace.

The engine will scan your file, match the original lyrics to the rows on your screen, and instantly populate all the text boxes with your custom data. Hit **Save Changes** and you are good to go!

title: Ambient Mode: Floating Lyrics Canvas
summary: Turn your monitor into a relaxing lyric waterfall with Ambient Mode.
content:
Sometimes you just want to put on a playlist and zone out without staring at a grid of album covers. 

We built **Ambient Mode** for exactly this reason.

---

## 1. Entering Ambient Mode

To activate it, head over to the **Settings** tab and click **Enter Ambient View**. 

The entire dashboard UI (the search bar, the song cards, the categories) will vanish. All that remains is the deep dynamic background and the player controls at the bottom of the screen.

## 2. The Lyric Waterfall

While Ambient Mode is active, the app silently scans your entire Vault in the background. It extracts random, perfectly synced lyric fragments and ad-libs from your saved songs.

These fragments are then spawned at the bottom of the screen as chat bubbles. The bubbles float gracefully upwards, showcasing the artist's profile picture alongside the lyric and its translation.

It is the perfect screensaver for a secondary monitor or a TV!

title: Mobile Optimization: PlanetMusic on the Go
summary: How the interface and workspaces dynamically adapt to fit perfectly on your mobile device.
content:
Using the studio on your phone? You might think a heavy app with syncing and translation engines would struggle on mobile screens. However, the architecture of the workspaces ensure everything runs smoothly.

---

## 1. The Fluid Song Modal

When you open a song on a desktop, you get a clean split-screen layout with the album art on the left and the lyrics on the right. 

On mobile, the modal intelligently stacks everything into a single scrolling vertical column. The album art and controls stick neatly to the top, while the lyrics expand to fill the rest of the vertical space below.

## 2. Workspace Adaptability

The complex grid layouts in the Translation Workspace and Creator Studio break down into highly readable, single-column rows. 

Even the Sync Workspace, with its dense matrix of timing buttons, reorganizes itself. The alignment of the keyboard emulation buttons allow you to tap the up and down arrows with your thumbs just as easily as hitting the spacebar on a laptop.

Wherever you go, your entire Vault is ready for you in the palm of your hand!

title: How to Contact Us & Get Support
summary: Having trouble with your Vault or spotted a bug? Here is how to reach the developers.
content:
Have a question, feedback, or a bug report? The Contact Tab is your direct line to us. 

---

## 1. Sending a Message

Navigate to the **Contact** tab in the main navigation bar. You will find a simple, secure form where you can type out your issue. 

The team of developers read every message that comes through the pipeline to ensure we are constantly improving the app.

## 2. A Crucial Rule for Replies

Because we deeply respect your privacy and operate a zero-tracking policy, the contact form does not force you to enter an email address to submit a message. 

But here is the catch: **if you want us to reach back to you, you must provide your email address directly in the message body.**

A massive influx of feedback messages arrive every week. If you ask a question but leave no contact info in the text box, we have absolutely no way to send you an answer!

Please be specific in your messages, and we will get back to you as soon as we can.
